name: CapCut Adaptive Texture Caption Animation
use_when: A social edit needs captions that feel integrated with the footage rather than plain static subtitles.
The background has enough contrast and texture for CapCut's caption animation to create a readable color/texture change.
The creator wants a quick stylized auto-caption treatment that can still be manually checked.
avoid_when: The footage is too busy, low contrast, or flickery for animated caption color/texture to stay readable.
The captions carry story-critical accessibility information and should remain stable.
Designed text, product UI, proof cards, or faces already compete for the caption region.

timeline_pattern.pattern: auto_captions -> apply_style_to_all -> choose_clean_font -> slight_character_tightening -> caption_animation_preset -> reposition -> phone_size_qc
timeline_pattern.preset_rule: CapCut caption animations such as Single Line, Negative Grow, Multi Line, and Multi Line 3 can create background-reactive color/texture looks; test each against the actual footage.
timeline_pattern.font_rule: Use a readable sans font before applying the animation; expressive fonts make the preset harder to QC.
timeline_pattern.manual_review_rule: Auto captions remain drafts until wording, timing, line breaks, and safe placement are corrected.

motion.rule: Caption animation must finish before the viewer needs to read the word and should not compete with other motion.

keyframe_values.tracking: A small CapCut Character value around -1 can tighten large captions when it does not cause collisions or shimmer.
keyframe_values.preset_choice: Single Line is a clean starting point; compare alternate presets only if the hierarchy remains readable.

sound.rule: No SFX is required for continuous caption texture; speech clarity is the priority.

captions.rule: Apply to all only after testing the style on bright, dark, busy, and face-heavy frames.

color.rule: The background-reactive color/texture must preserve caption edge contrast on the actual footage.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use ASS subtitles or drawtext with styled foreground/background changes only if the exact treatment is specified; otherwise approximate with readable static captions and contact-sheet QC.
implementation.remotion: Represent captionStyle with font, letterSpacing, animationPreset, safeRegion, and per-frame contrast checks against the video background.
implementation.blender: Use text objects or composited captions with animated materials only for controlled renders; inspect against the final footage.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Generate auto captions, select Apply To All, choose a readable font, optionally set Character around -1, apply a caption animation such as Single Line, Negative Grow, Multi Line, or Multi Line 3, then reposition and review every caption.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Create captions, upgrade selected captions to graphics only after correction, then apply a tested text animation or style preset while preserving contrast.

common_mistakes: Applying the preset to all captions before correcting the transcript.
Letting the animated caption texture disappear on bright or busy backgrounds.
Using tight character spacing on small subtitles until letters collide.
Keeping stylized captions over faces, product UI, proof, or other designed text.
Using the effect for serious or accessibility-first sections where stable subtitles are better.
qc: Are auto-caption words, timing, and line breaks corrected?
Does every caption remain readable on bright, dark, and busy frames?
Does caption animation finish before the word needs to be read?
Do captions avoid faces, product UI, proof, and designed text?
Does the style still work when previewed at phone size?
